It is actually, There is no evidence whatsoever in the climatic records that CO2 levels in the atmosphere have driven global temperature. All the recent warm spells took place with CO2 stable. If we go back thousands of years there's no evidence of CO2 increasing causing the Earth to warm. I believe there's a reasonable explanation to that, and NASA keeps telling us but if you're not aware you don't notice their message. Water vapour a GHG is 4% of the atmosphere in the Tropics, which is approximately 100 times the CO2 in the atmosphere WV + CO2 = 100% of the GHGs. Water vapour is 40000ppm, CO2 is 425ppm. In terms of GHG WV is absolutely dominant, and changes in the level of CO2 are trivial in terms of the total GHGs in the Tropics. Hansen et al, 1981 actually told us this: “The history of the warming obviously does not follow the course of the CO2 increase indicating that other factors must affect the global mean temperatures.” Science, August 1981, Volume 213, Number 4511. J Hansen, D. Johnson, A. Lacis, S. Lebedeff. P.Lee, D. Rind, G. Russell. (Hansen et al. 1981), Volume, 213, No. 4511 Climate Impact of Increasing Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide. But it appears no one was listening

I noticed earlier that Google Maps finally made its way into Google AI Studio. That reminded me of Pietro Miotti's experiment, where he used 48 AI agents and NASA LiDAR data to scan over 1,200 km² of jungle for potential archaeological structures. Naturally, I started wondering: what if we built a platform to do something similar, but at a global scale? A few experiments later, meet TerraPulse LiDAR 🌍 A global geospatial exploration platform that combines Google Maps, NASA LiDAR datasets, satellite imagery and terrain analysis to discover potential archaeological sites, assess existing survey coverage and prioritize new LiDAR missions. Built with Google AI Studio, Google Maps Platform and NASA Earthdata. What else is hiding beneath the surface?
